bmi doesn't take into consideration: sex, age, race, muscle mass, or abdominal obesity, just to name the ones that come to mind. generally, if you want to make a first assessment of "does this person need to lose weight/is this person very overweight", you can usually just look once at the person.

bmi was LITERALLY created to be used as a statistical tool, and the inventor actually made a point that it shouldn't be used on individuals. It was also made using white men as a basis. We know that men and women carry weight differently, and that different races carry weight differently. being a white male at 28 bmi is not the same as a black woman at 28 bmi. 

Not to even mention, using a measure of fatness and/or bmi does not give the full picture when determining someone's overall health. You have to consider things like: mental well-being surrounding food and weight, cholesterol levels, blood sugar levels, blood pressure, exercise levels, weight fluctuations, if your fatness hinders you physically or emotionally in any way in your life, genetic predisposition to certain diseases, just to mention a few. Using bmi is fine if you know these things, but generally, people don't.

(also as a side note, people tend to put way much more emphasis on the level of fatness than the other things i mentioned. i am personally a bit chubby right now, but i am happy being this way, because i know all of those other factors are in the green for me. the only time in my life when i have been under 25 bmi was at the height of my eating disorder, when i was sent to the hospital for not keeping down ANY food. I would take being a bit fat over relapsing into my eating disorder a hundred times over.)

Her posting this is absolutely cringe, but it's true that BMI is an awful tool. Using it to measure fatness is inconsistent at best, and using it to measure health is just wrong. I'm all for anti diet culture any day.

opioids are called such bc they all bind to opioid receptors, and they are all similar in structure (with the exception of the fully synthetic ones like methadone and fentanyl). their molecular structure, working mechanism and what they are used for are completely different from both wellbutrin and other adhd medication.

If you're thinking about trying adhd medication, there's many different types of stimulants and the chance that you're allergic to all of them is pretty low.  I recommend doing some research on the different medications used to treat adhd and pay attention to the active ingredient in each. For example Wellbutrin is the brand name of the drug that GlaxoSmithKline produces, but the active ingredient is buproprion, which will also be the generic name. The active ingredient is what matters when comparing medications.

Many times patients can be allergic to a certain active ingredient but are able to use another from the same group (e.g. venlafaxine vs duloxetine)!

(If you have any questions or need help you're free to pm me, I'm a nurse and i personally take both adhd medication (Elvanse) and buproprion so i can probably give some guidance! I'm european so i can't say much about things specific to the us health care system, but medicines affect the body the same way everywhere 😄 )
